events.subtitle: Jobim Centennial Celebration
events.factual_description: Wolf Trap presents Eliane Elias: Jobim Centennial Celebration at The Barns in Vienna, Virginia on Saturday, April 3, 2027 at 7:30 PM; doors open at 6:00 PM. The program honors the 100th birthday of Antonio Carlos Jobim and features Elias with bassist Marc Johnson, Brazilian drummer/percussionist Rafael Barata, and guitarist Leandro Pellegrino. Wolf Trap says the set includes Jobim classics such as The Girl from Ipanema and Desafinado alongside music from Elias's current repertoire. Jazz at Lincoln Center independently lists the same quartet and Jobim-centennial program in January 2027, confirming this as a touring centennial project rather than a one-off local production.

en.why_it_matters: Elias has spent decades making Brazilian song and modern jazz feel like one language, and Jobim is unusually well matched to both sides of her playing. The attraction here is not simply a centennial label: Marc Johnson gives the harmony real depth, Rafael Barata brings a Brazilian rhythmic vocabulary that can stay supple rather than decorative, and the scale of The Barns should keep the piano-guitar-rhythm conversation close enough to hear the details. It is a strong way to hear a living Brazilian master engage repertoire that sits near the center of her musical identity.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for this one if the local calendar is open. The Barns is an unusually good scale for the quartet, and the Jobim centennial gives the program a clear reason to exist now. Because the same project is traveling to other major jazz venues, there is useful flexibility rather than a need to rebuild larger travel plans around this single stop.

es.why_it_matters: Elias lleva décadas haciendo que la canción brasileña y el jazz moderno suenen como un solo idioma, y Jobim cae justo en el centro de esas dos vertientes. Lo atractivo no es nada más la etiqueta del centenario: Marc Johnson le da profundidad armónica al grupo, Rafael Barata aporta un lenguaje rítmico brasileño que puede mantenerse flexible y no ornamental, y la escala de The Barns debería dejar muy cerca la conversación entre piano, guitarra y sección rítmica. Es una muy buena forma de escuchar a una maestra brasileña viva trabajando un repertorio que forma parte central de su identidad musical.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente si la fecha está libre. The Barns tiene una escala especialmente buena para este cuarteto y el centenario de Jobim le da al programa una razón clara para existir ahora. Como el mismo proyecto estará pasando por otros recintos importantes de jazz, hay margen real para escoger sin tener que rehacer planes mayores alrededor de esta sola parada.
